question: What mechanisms drive re-entrant phase transitions in systems with paramagnetic ligands?
answer: Sequential structural phase transitions drive the re-entrant phase behavior in the lanthanum complex.  At low temperatures, diamagnetic π-radical dimers, called "pancake bonds," exist. Upon heating, these dimers rupture in two steps, leading to increased magnetic moments as unpaired electrons become available. This is accompanied by crystallographic space group changes from C2/c to P1 and back to C2/c.  A theoretical model suggests that competition between magnetic interactions within the dimers and the flexibility of the surrounding molecular network stabilizes a lower-symmetry triclinic phase at intermediate temperatures, causing the re-entrant behavior.

### Task 1: Summarize the Purpose of the Paper  
The paper investigates π-π radical interactions and their role in supramolecular recognition, focusing on their ability to induce switchable structural and magnetic properties. By studying the La(hfac)₃(pyDTDA)₂ coordination complex, the authors observe rare re-entrant phase transitions driven by "pancake bonding" between π-radical ligands. The paper develops a theoretical model that explains this behavior and extends the findings to predict re-entrant phase transitions in other systems with low lattice rigidity.
